physics_goals.quote: This, in particular, gives us possibility to perform measurements of masses of elementary particles with high precision.
physics_goals.value: Precise mass measurements of elementary particles (psi family, D mesons, tau lepton) using precision beam-energy calibration, and measurement of R

summary.plain: The universal magnetic detector at the Budker Institute's VEPP-4M collider in Novosibirsk, taking data since 2002. Because the beam energy is calibrated to about one part in a million by resonant depolarisation, KEDR measured the J/psi, psi(2S) and D meson masses and the tau lepton mass with record precision.
summary.technical: KEDR at VEPP-4M (2E = 2-11 GeV): vertex detector, central drift chamber, aerogel Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight counters, liquid-krypton and CsI calorimeters, muon system and superconducting coil; beam energy by resonant depolarisation (~0.001%) and Compton backscattering (~0.003%); psi region until 2018, R scan 4.6-7 GeV 2018-2020; spokesman V. E. Blinov.

unique_capabilities.quote: the precision calibration of energy of beams by means of the resonant depolarization method (accuracy ~0.001%) and the method of Compton backscattering (accuracy ~0.003%) is used
unique_capabilities.value: Beam-energy calibration by resonant depolarisation (accuracy about 0.001%) and Compton backscattering (about 0.003%)
